description: Finding surfaced during Arc 2 (stoa--xyb.6, PR #25 cd827d7, 2026-05-23). On Windows, 'git worktree remove' can de-register a worktree (so 'git worktree list' reports it gone) yet FAIL to delete the directory with Permission denied, leaving an ORPHAN DIR invisible to the registration view. §5.10 verify-before-claim caught it because PLINY verified the dir was actually gone (not just the registration); rm -rf cleaned it. PROPOSED FIX: §5.10 signoff cleanup (and/or the Arc-3 enforcement-layer clean-tree hook) should explicitly assert the worktree DIR is removed, not just the registration. N=1 (first observation). Accrete per §15 / op-disc §6.7.1; fold into a future substrate arc. Empirical anchor: stoa--xyb.6 close verdict 2026-05-23T08:06:52Z.

comments.text: N=2: recurred in Arc 3 Stage 1 close (PR #26 0ad68db, 2026-05-23). This time 'git worktree remove' hit Windows 'Device or resource busy' on the dir delete (Arc 2 was 'Permission denied') — same failure class: registration de-registered but dir persisted; retry cleared it; §5.10 verify-before-claim caught it again. Two distinct error strings (Permission denied / Device or resource busy), same orphan-dir pattern, two consecutive arcs. Pattern is real + recurring; the §5.10 verify-before-claim discipline is reliably catching it (no silent failure), but the cleanup itself should retry-and-verify-dir-gone. Promote from N=1 to N=2 evidence for a future hardening arc.

title: Windows: git worktree remove de-registers but leaves orphan dir (Permission-denied on dir delete) — §5.10 cleanup should verify dir-gone, not just registration
